# `nlink-lab stats`

What the lab's nodes use, from their cgroups (containers, and namespace nodes with `cpu`/`memory` limits) — or, for one node with `--pid`, `--procs` or `--pidfile-glob`, what its processes use, from `/proc` (RSS, PSS, open fds, CPU ticks).

```bash
nlink-lab stats
sudo nlink-lab stats site_a --procs --watch 2s
sudo nlink-lab --json stats site_a --pid 4242 | jq '.processes[0].pss_kb'
```

## Reference

<!-- cli-ref:start (generated by `nlink-lab docs-gen`; do not edit) -->

```text
What nodes use (cgroup v2: CPU time, memory, PIDs) — or with `--pid`, `--procs` or `--pidfile-glob`, what a node's processes use.

Process samples read `/proc/<pid>/{stat,status,smaps_rollup}` and count `/proc/<pid>/fd/` (root: the fd directory is 0700); on a container node they are routed through the runtime. Sum `pss_kb`, not `rss_kb`, to get a node's memory: RSS counts every shared page once per process. CPU ticks are `sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK)` units (usually 100 per second). `--watch` samples again until Ctrl-C.

JSON OUTPUT: { "schema_version": 1, "lab", "nodes": [ { "node", "kind", "cpu_usec", "memory_bytes", "memory_max", "cpu_max", "pids" } ] }, or with process flags { "schema_version": 1, "lab", "node", "processes": [ { "node", "host_pid", "ns_pid", "name"?, "command", "uid", "rss_kb"?, "vsz_kb"?, "pss_kb"?, "fd_count", "cpu_user_ticks", "cpu_kernel_ticks", "started_at_unix_micros", "state" } ] } Schemas: docs/json-schemas/stats.schema.json, stats-procs.schema.json

Usage: nlink-lab stats [OPTIONS] [NODE]

Arguments:
  [NODE]
          One node (default: every node with a cgroup: containers and cpu/memory-limited namespace nodes)

Options:
  -L, --lab <LAB>
          The lab. Default: `$NLINK_LAB`, then the one `nlink-lab use` selected, then the only running lab

      --pid <PID>
          Sample this process of NODE, by the PID the node sees (the host's on a namespace node, the container's own on a container node; repeatable)

      --procs
          Sample every process in NODE's network namespace

      --pidfile-glob <PATTERN>
          Sample the processes NODE's pidfiles name: every file matching this absolute path, whose file name may hold `*` and `?` (`'/run/*.pid'`). Each record's `name` is the pidfile's stem; a stale pidfile is skipped

      --watch <DURATION>
          Sample again at this interval until Ctrl-C (`--format ndjson`: one document per sample)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```
